chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: Slow songs, features and his opening tune
summary: He features I Cover the Waterfront and I'm Confessin', likes fast and slow, and opens with Even When You're Smiling.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: What kind of slow songs do you like to play on the trombone?
'I Cover the Waterfront' and 'Dear old Southland'
How would you describe, what would you say was your strongest point?

What would you say was your strongest point, playing a ballad or playing fast ... like Don Byas was known for his execution and how fast he could play Cherokee and stuff like that. And Jimmy Harrison ... he liked fast things.
I like fast and slow. ... just like I'm Cover the Waterfront, I would not have used that tune for nothing. That's the most beautiful tune they were going to play and Confessin. "Confessin'"
Do you think that a ballad, that you're stronger at playing ballads than something fast?
No, it don't make no difference. I don't get tired when I start playing like that.
No, I'm not talking about tired. I'm talking about which do you think you're best, that you project your emotions better in a ballad or blues or something fast.
That's what you groove behind, you can play that best?
Even When You're Smiling. that's my opening tune.
'When You're Smiling,' that's your opening tune you say?
